fn merge_sorted(xs: List[Int], ys: List[Int]) -> List[Int]
  requires sorted(xs)
  requires sorted(ys)
  ensures len(result) == len(xs) + len(ys)
  ensures sorted(result)
  ensures forall x in xs: contains(result, x)
  ensures forall y in ys: contains(result, y)
  effects pure
  example merge_sorted([1, 4, 9], [2, 3]) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 9]
  example merge_sorted([], [5, 6]) == [5, 6]
  example merge_sorted([1, 2, 3], []) == [1, 2, 3]
  example merge_sorted([], []) == []
{
  match xs {
    [] => ys
    [hx, ..tx] => match ys {
      [] => xs
      [hy, ..ty] => if hx <= hy then [hx] ++ merge_sorted(tx, ys) else [hy] ++ merge_sorted(xs, ty)
    }
  }
}

fn max(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
  requires true
  ensures result >= a and result >= b
  ensures result == a or result == b
  effects pure
  example max(1, 2) == 2
  example max(5, 5) == 5
  example max(-3, -7) == -3
{
  if a >= b then a else b
}

fn count_eq(xs: List[Int], v: Int) -> Int
  requires true
  ensures result == count(xs, v)
  effects pure
  example count_eq([1, 2, 2, 3], 2) == 2
  example count_eq([], 5) == 0
  example count_eq([7], 7) == 1
{
  match xs {
    [] => 0
    [h, ..t] => if h == v then 1 + count_eq(t, v) else count_eq(t, v)
  }
}

fn best_count(xs: List[Int]) -> Int
  requires true
  ensures (len(xs) == 0 and result == 0) or (len(xs) > 0 and result >= 1)
  ensures forall x in xs: count(xs, x) <= result
  ensures len(xs) == 0 or (exists x in xs: count(xs, x) == result)
  effects pure
  example best_count([]) == 0
  example best_count([1, 2, 2, 3]) == 2
  example best_count([5]) == 1
{
  match xs {
    [] => 0
    [h, ..t] => max(count_eq(xs, h), best_count(t))
  }
}

fn find_most_frequent(all: List[Int], remaining: List[Int], target: Int) -> Int
  requires exists x in remaining: count(all, x) == target
  ensures count(all, result) == target
  effects pure
  example find_most_frequent([1, 2, 2, 3], [1, 2, 2, 3], 2) == 2
  example find_most_frequent([5], [5], 1) == 5
{
  match remaining {
    [] => 0
    [h, ..t] => if count_eq(all, h) == target then h else find_most_frequent(all, t, target)
  }
}

fn most_frequent(xs: List[Int]) -> Option[Int]
  requires true
  ensures len(xs) > 0 or result == None
  ensures len(xs) == 0 or (exists v in xs: result == Some(v) and count_eq(xs, v) == best_count(xs))
  effects pure
  example most_frequent([1, 2, 2, 3]) == Some(2)
  example most_frequent([]) == None
  example most_frequent([4, 4, 4, 1, 2]) == Some(4)
  example most_frequent([9]) == Some(9)
{
  match xs {
    [] => None
    [h, ..t] => Some(find_most_frequent(xs, xs, best_count(xs)))
  }
}
